channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Two Former Commanders Arrested in Connection with Kyrgyz Military Helicopter Crash
item.description: Two former commanders of the Kyrgyz Air Force, including ex-commander Kylychbek Aidaraliev and a unit commander Daniyar Davitahunov, have been arrested. They face charges related to violating flight safety regulations, leading to a fatal Mi-8MTV helicopter crash in January 2024. Both have been detained until December 2026.

item.title: Taliban Minister of Industry and Commerce meets Tanzania's Minister of Minerals to boost trade
item.description: Nooruddin Azizi, the Taliban's Minister of Industry and Commerce, met with Tanzania's Minister of Minerals, Anthony Mavunde, to discuss expanding bilateral trade. Discussions included exporting Afghan agricultural products, carpets, and minerals to Tanzania, and holding trade exhibitions. Processing mineral resources within Afghanistan was also considered.

item.title: Taliban Claim Over 200 Media Outlets Licensed in Past Five Years
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Information and Culture claims over 200 media outlets have received operating licenses in Afghanistan in the last five years. A spokesperson stated the ministry is launching programs to support media growth and improve journalists' capacities. However, many media outlets have shut down and journalists lost jobs since the Taliban's return to power.

item.title: Activists Urge UN to Secure Release of Detained University Lecturer
item.description: Former university professors, writers, and activists are calling on UN human rights bodies to secure the immediate release of Din Mohammad Javid, a private university lecturer. His family has no information on his whereabouts, legal status, or condition. Concerns about arbitrary detention and enforced disappearance have been raised due to his medical needs.

item.title: Moscow Reviews Efforts to Resolve Afghanistan-Pakistan Tensions
item.description: Discussions were held in Moscow regarding efforts to resolve tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan. The review of these diplomatic efforts took place amidst ongoing regional developments and bilateral relations between the two neighboring countries.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence Development and Digital Space Protection Discussed
item.description: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence presents both opportunities and challenges. While AI is increasingly integrated into various sectors, concerns arise regarding data privacy, misinformation, deepfakes, and cyberattacks. International cooperation is deemed crucial for regulating AI, balancing innovation with human rights and digital security.

item.title: Uzbekneftegaz to Double Gasoline Supply to Exchange Amid Rising Demand
item.description: Uzbekneftegaz plans to increase daily gasoline supply to the exchange to 8,000 tons, potentially up to 10,000 tons if demand continues to grow. The company currently offers 4,600 tons daily. This move aims to stabilize prices, which have been influenced by increased demand and precautionary buying by gas stations.

item.title: Documentary Evidence of Hazara Genocide and Forced Displacement Presented to European Parliament
item.description: Documentary evidence and reports concerning the 'genocide' and forced displacement of the Hazara people have been presented to the European Parliament. The specific details of the presentation and the content of the evidence were not disclosed.

item.title: Mass Youth Protests Erupt Across Over 25 European Countries
item.description: Tens of thousands of young people have protested in over 25 European countries against the rising cost of living, tuition fees, and underfunding of education. Protesters demanded increased funding for schools and universities, better living conditions, and action against unemployment and climate change. Some protests involved property damage.

item.title: Modern Youth Face New Challenges in Pursuit of Financial Independence and Housing
item.description: Today's youth, despite greater access to education and information, face significant hurdles to financial independence. High competition, job scarcity, and the difficulty of gaining experience delay financial self-sufficiency. Additionally, rising housing costs and rents make homeownership increasingly unattainable for many young people.

item.title: Over 144 Rights Groups Protest France's Potential Engagement with Taliban
item.description: More than 144 Afghan human rights and civil society organizations have protested France's potential consular engagement with the Taliban and a recent ICC decision. They argue the ICC decision could undermine justice for victims and urged France not to normalize the Taliban's repression or transfer consular affairs of Afghan missions.

item.title: Russia Urges Regional Cooperation Against Afghan Militant Groups
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated that militant groups like ISKP and TTP remain active in Afghanistan, posing a regional security threat. Moscow advocates for a common goal in counter-terrorism, emphasizing economic development and institutional strengthening in Afghanistan. Russia also supports a diplomatic solution to tensions between Pakistan and the Taliban government.

item.title: Europe's Generation Z Protests Rising Costs, Education Funding, and Gaza Conflict
item.description: Young people across 25 European countries have taken to the streets to protest against the rising cost of living, increased tuition fees, and underfunding of education. Protesters also voiced opposition to their governments' stances on the conflict in Gaza.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Recalculate Electricity Bills for Homes Lacking Gas Supply from November 25
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Energy announced that electricity bills for residents in areas without gas supply will be recalculated starting November 25. This adjustment follows complaints about the standard electricity tariff being applied instead of the preferential rate for unsupplied gas areas.

item.title: Astana Hospitals See Surge in Respiratory Illnesses, Primarily Affecting Children
item.description: Astana is experiencing a rise in acute respiratory viral infections and influenza cases, with 313 patients currently hospitalized. A significant majority, 220, are children, and 30 are pregnant women. Hospital bed capacity has been increased, and emergency services are operating on an enhanced schedule.

item.title: Former Khorezm Employment Center Official Detained in Turkey
item.description: A citizen of Uzbekistan, wanted internationally, has been detained in Turkey. The former official from the Khorezm Region Employment Promotion Center is accused of embezzling state funds and falsifying documents. She was apprehended through a joint operation by Uzbek and Turkish law enforcement.

item.title: Uzbekistan Increases Preferential Electricity Tariff for Undersupplied Areas
item.description: Starting November 1, households in areas not supplied with natural gas or with limited gas supply in Uzbekistan will pay 650 soums per kilowatt-hour for electricity up to 350 kWh. This preferential rate will be applied automatically without requiring additional applications. The change aims to support residents in regions facing gas shortages.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Fund Cancer Treatment Through Medical Insurance from 2027
item.description: Starting in 2027, Uzbekistan will shift its state funding for cancer care to a medical insurance system. The Medical Insurance Fund will cover costs for diagnostics, surgeries, medications, and other treatments within the guaranteed package. This change aims to improve access to and financing of oncology services for patients.

item.title: Uzbek national suspected of embezzlement arrested in Turkey and extradited
item.description: A former employee of an employment assistance structure in Uzbekistan's Khorezm region, who was on an international wanted list, has been apprehended in Turkey. She was extradited to Uzbekistan and is suspected of embezzling state funds and forging documents using her official position. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Sending Skilled Workers to Australian Labor Market
item.description: Uzbekistan has initiated practical discussions with representatives of Australia's Northern Territory regarding the export of skilled labor. The talks, facilitated by the Uzbek embassy in Singapore, focused on identifying Australia's needs, particularly in the oil and gas sector, and establishing mechanisms for legal employment of Uzbek citizens. Both sides also agreed to hold consular consultations to protect the rights of their citizens.

item.title: Astana Introduces Designated Fire Truck Access Zones in Residential Areas
item.description: Astana is establishing special zones around apartment buildings to ensure fire trucks can access upper floors during emergencies. A demonstration of one such zone at the 'Grand Alatau' complex was held with the participation of the Minister of Emergency Situations. New construction standards in Kazakhstan now mandate these fire access paths, specifying distances from building facades based on height.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ministry: Wildberries Not Under EU Sanctions Despite Founder's Inclusion
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy and Commerce stated that sanctions imposed by the EU are against an individual, not the Wildberries marketplace itself. The ministry, along with the National Bank, is monitoring financial transactions to prevent sanctions circumvention. Wildberries founder Tatyana Kim resigned as CEO but will remain involved in strategic development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Faces Single International Internet Traffic Operator
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is left with only one operator for international internet traffic. This consolidation raises concerns about the country's digital infrastructure and connectivity.

item.title: Sar-e Pol Declared Second Mine-Free Province in Afghanistan
item.description: Afghanistan's National Disaster Management Authority, now under Taliban control, has declared Sar-e Pol province free of mines and explosive materials. This follows a similar declaration for Bamyan province, marking the end of 36 years of demining operations.

item.title: Afghan Women Face Healthcare Crisis as Hundreds of Clinics Close
item.description: Nearly 300 health facilities in Afghanistan have closed or suspended services this year, impacting over one million women and girls. UN Women reports that funding cuts and Taliban bans on female health workers exacerbate the crisis, leaving many without essential care.

item.title: Uzbekistan Identifies Lack of Information as Key Barrier to Free Healthcare
item.description: Many in Uzbekistan struggle to access free medical care not due to organizational issues, but a lack of awareness about available services and where to seek them. The State Medical Insurance Fund highlights that informing citizens is crucial for improving access.

item.title: OTP Group Acquires Remaining State Shares in Ipoteka Bank, Increasing Stake to 90.4%
item.description: Hungary's OTP Group is acquiring the remaining approximately 17.5% of state shares in Ipoteka Bank. Following the transaction, OTP Group's stake will reach 90.4%. Since joining OTP Group in June 2023, Ipoteka Bank has undergone significant transformation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Greenhouse Owners Seek More Time to Abandon Coal Heating
item.description: Greenhouse owners in Uzbekistan are requesting an extension beyond the December 1st deadline to switch from coal to gas, electricity, or other renewable energy sources. They cite difficulties in meeting strict emission standards for continued coal use and challenges with liquefied gas conversion.

item.title: International Kurash Tournament Held in Termez, Uzbekistan
item.description: An international open Kurash tournament dedicated to the memory of Al-Hakim at-Termizi is underway in Termez. Organized following a presidential decree, the event features over 15 countries and 100 Uzbek athletes competing in three weight categories. The prize fund is $42,000 USD.

item.title: Uzbekistan Unveils Plan for Transition to Revised Latin Alphabet
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Justice has released a draft resolution for public discussion on transitioning all sectors to a revised Latin alphabet. The plan outlines a phased adoption for government bodies, educational institutions, and media, with the new alphabet to take effect April 22, 2027.

item.title: Head of Electronic Technology Development Center Sentenced to 15 Years
item.description: Omоnillokhon Khodjiakbarov, head of Uzbekistan's Center for the Development of Electronic Technologies, has been sentenced to 15 years in prison. A military court found the major general guilty of disclosing state secrets and abusing his official powers.

item.title: Uzbekistan Health Insurance Fund Explains Regional Free Medicine Access Difficulties
item.description: Residents in Uzbekistan's regions face challenges accessing free medicines due to uneven pharmacy network development, despite unified state medical insurance rules. The Health Insurance Fund noted that while Tashkent has the highest availability, the system is uniform nationwide. Addressing the issue requires developing the pharmacy network alongside funding.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Drug Testing for Civil Servants
item.description: Kazakhstan has implemented a new procedure for drug testing civil servants. Officials exhibiting suspicious behavior, such as unexplained absences or mood swings, may be sent for medical examination. Refusal to undergo testing or a positive result can lead to dismissal from service.

item.title: New Epilepsy Treatment Method Successfully Applied in Aktobe
item.description: The first surgery to implant a vagus nerve stimulator (VNS) for epilepsy treatment has been performed in Aktobe, Kazakhstan. The high-tech operation was conducted by specialists at the regional hospital in collaboration with doctors from the National Center for Neurosurgery in Astana. This advanced treatment is now accessible locally.

item.title: Four Kazakh Students Detained in Slovakia on Suspicion of Kidnapping
item.description: Four citizens of Kazakhstan have been detained in Slovakia on suspicion of kidnapping. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed consular and legal assistance is being provided. Reports indicate the students allegedly broke into a home, impersonated special forces, and assaulted a resident while demanding money.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sambo Team Secures First Place at SCO Open Tournament
item.description: The Uzbekistan national sambo team, comprising seven athletes, achieved first place overall at the SCO Open Tournament in Moscow. They secured seven medals, including four gold, one silver, and two bronze, outperforming competitors from ten countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kazhydromet Warns of Air Pollution Risk in Ten Cities
item.description: Kazhydromet has issued a warning for unfavorable meteorological conditions in ten Kazakh cities on Sunday, November 22. These conditions can lead to the accumulation of pollutants near the ground. PM2.5, nitrogen dioxide, and hydrogen sulfide exceedances were previously recorded.

item.title: Uzbekistan's exports grew 33 percent in Jan-Oct 2026, Trend reports
item.description: Uzbekistan's exports, excluding special exports, increased by 33 percent year-on-year to $25.7 billion in January-October 2026, according to Azerbaijani agency Trend. Foreign investment and loans reached $49.5 billion. Uzbekistan aims to join the WTO in 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Hungary discuss cooperation in legal education
item.description: Uzbekistan and Hungary have discussed expanding cooperation in legal education. A delegation visited Hungary to study advanced foreign experience and strengthen ties with international institutions. Discussions included academic exchange and joint educational programs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations Saved 428 Lives in First 10 Months
item.description: In the first 10 months of the year, Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations (MES) received over 2.79 million appeals from citizens. MES rescuers saved 428 lives, including victims of road accidents, drownings, mountain incidents, and fires. Additionally, first aid was provided to 731 individuals before medical personnel arrived. The ministry also conducted significant work on cleaning water bodies and flood protection.
